newsitem.title: UK: LME copper still tight, zinc advance continues.
newsitem.headline: LME copper still tight, zinc advance continues.

text.p: Nearby tightness plaguing the copper market last week reared its head again on Monday as the "tomorrow/next day" traded up to the London Metal Exchange (LME) limit during the midday ring.
Zinc, meanwhile, cruised to new seven year highs despite being technically overbought, against a background of constructive fundamentals and keen speculative interest.
It ended the midday kerb at $1,542 per tonne, a fresh high since August 1990 and up $18 from Friday's finish.
"Once it catches fire zinc can run and run," a trader said. "There's no obvious resistance for some way above here."
Flagship copper was also firmer at $2,333, up $17, underpinned by the flaring backwardation and boosted by short covering after Friday's technically constructive close, traders said.

Borrowing of cash/August in the pre-market and August/threes dates in the rings widened the spread to $140/$150 after it initally contracted in early inter-office trading to around $125/$135, traders said.
"It looks like things are rolling forward a bit, at least to the end of the month," one trader said.
In the first ring "tom/next" traded up to $24, the LME-imposed limit of one percent of the previous day's cash settlement prices. Meanwhile cash/day traded at $21 in the second ring.
But three months prices were being capped by resistance at $2,335 for now although a breach of that level would target $2,360, analysts said.
Aluminium benefitted from the upward moves of copper and zinc, and prices ended firmer at $1,616, up $8.50. But resistance was in evidence in the $1,620 area.
Generally volumes were quite light in all the metals, reflecting the seasonal slow period, traders said.
Lead pushed higher, boosted by strength in zinc, and finished at $655 versus $648/$649. Overhead resistance at $660 was the next target, followed by recent highs of $675, analysts said.
Nickel was firmer with the others, swinging back above $6,800 but prices still looked locked in a downtrend, traders said. Prices were last at $6,810, up $70.
Tin, the complex's weakling in recent days, languished in a tight range near recent 2-1/3 year lows.
It was last barely changed at $5,440, down $20, while alloy was very quiet.
